expertInsight: The questions that catch people out are usually about entitlement processes and milestones: when a milestone starts, when it pauses, and what happens when a case changes status. Many scenarios also give you several routing tools that would all work, and the right answer is the simplest one that meets the need. Read for the exact requirement, such as by skill, by queue or by customer tier, before choosing between assignment rules, Omni-Channel queues and skills-based routing.

examFormat.heading: Service Cloud Consultant Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: You can take the exam online with a proctor or at a test centre. Here is what to expect:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Most questions describe a support team with a specific problem, such as missed response times or cases going to the wrong team, and ask for the best setup.
bestWayToPass: Know your routing options: Assignment rules, queues, Omni-Channel and skills-based routing each fit different needs.
Learn entitlements well: Entitlement processes, milestones, and what starts, pauses and completes them.
Understand knowledge: Article types, data categories, and how articles reach agents, bots and customers.

keyConcepts.h2: Service Cloud Consultant: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Case Management: Origins, Assignment, and Escalation
blocks.body: Cases can come in through email (**Email-to-Case**), web forms (**Web-to-Case**), phone, chat, messaging and self-service sites. The **case origin** field records the channel. **Assignment rules** decide which user or queue gets a new case, based on its fields. **Escalation rules** move cases or alert people if they stay open too long. **Auto-response rules** send the customer a first reply. Record types and support processes let different teams use different case statuses.

blocks.heading: Entitlements, Milestones, and Service Contracts
blocks.body: **Entitlements** say what support a customer is owed, such as phone support with a four-hour response. **Entitlement processes** are timelines of **milestones**, like first response and resolution, each with a time limit. **Milestone actions** send warnings or escalate when a milestone is close to or past its limit. Milestones can pause, for example while waiting on the customer, if the process is set up that way. **Service contracts** group entitlements for a customer, and can be linked to assets.

blocks.heading: Omni-Channel: Routing Models and Agent Capacity
blocks.body: **Omni-Channel** pushes work to available agents instead of agents picking from a list. **Queue-based routing** offers work to members of a queue. **Skills-based routing** matches work to agents with the right skills, like language or product. **Omni-Channel flows** let you route with logic. **Capacity** limits how much work an agent gets at once, and each work item uses some of that capacity. **Presence statuses** show what kind of work an agent can take. Omni Supervisor shows queues and agents in real time.

blocks.heading: Knowledge Management: Articles, Data Categories, and Case Deflection
blocks.body: **Salesforce Knowledge** stores articles that answer common questions. Articles go through draft, review and publish stages, and can be shown internally, to customers, to partners or publicly. **Data categories** organise articles and control who sees which ones. Agents see suggested articles on cases and can attach them. Customers find articles on help sites, and bots can suggest them in chat. When customers solve problems themselves, it is called **deflection**.

blocks.heading: Service Console: Macros, Quick Text, and Einstein Features
blocks.body: The **Service Console** lets agents work several cases in tabs, with related records alongside. **Macros** run a set of steps, like sending a reply and closing a case, with one click. **Quick text** inserts standard phrases. The **case feed** shows the history of emails, calls and updates in one place. AI features, including Einstein and Agentforce, can classify cases, suggest replies and articles, and summarise conversations, helping agents work faster.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Service Cloud Consultant Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Most questions give a support team, a problem, and several setups that might work. Choose the one that meets the exact need most simply.

blocks.heading: Case Routing: Which Tool When
blocks.body: Assignment rules for simple field-based assignment. Omni-Channel queues to push work to available agents. Skills-based routing when agents differ by skill.

blocks.heading: Knowledge Management
blocks.body: Use data categories to control who sees articles. Publish to the right audience: internal, customer, partner or public.

blocks.heading: Entitlements & SLAs
blocks.body: Entitlement processes hold milestones with time limits. Milestone actions warn or escalate before limits are missed.

blocks.heading: Omni-Channel Configuration
blocks.body: Set capacity and item size so agents get a manageable amount of work. Use presence statuses for each channel.

blocks.heading: Self-Service & Deflection
blocks.body: Help sites with good knowledge articles and bots answer simple questions, so agents can focus on harder ones.

sampleQuestions.question: Support emails should automatically become cases in Salesforce. What should be set up?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Email-to-Case turns incoming support emails into cases.
whyWrong: Articles answer questions, they don't create cases.
Escalation rules act on cases that already exist.
Web-to-Lead creates leads from a web form.

sampleQuestions.question: Gold customers must get a first response within one hour, and managers should be warned at 45 minutes. What should be used?
options: An entitlement process with a first response milestone and a warning action
sampleQuestions.explanation: Milestones track time limits, and milestone actions can warn before the limit is reached.
whyWrong: Assignment rules decide who gets the case, not response times.
Validation rules check data on save.
A queue holds cases but doesn't track service levels.

sampleQuestions.question: Cases should be pushed to the next available agent, with each agent handling up to three at a time. What fits?
options: Manual case picking from a list view
Omni-Channel with queue-based routing and agent capacity
sampleQuestions.explanation: Omni-Channel pushes work to available agents and uses capacity to limit how much each one gets.
whyWrong: Picking from a list isn't push routing and lets agents cherry-pick.
Assignment rules assign once and don't check availability or capacity.

sampleQuestions.question: French-speaking customers must be routed to agents who speak French. What should be used?
options: Queue-based routing to one shared queue
sampleQuestions.explanation: Skills-based routing matches work to agents who have the required skill, such as French.
whyWrong: Auto-response rules send replies to customers.
One shared queue offers work to anyone.

sampleQuestions.question: A case has been open for 48 hours with no update. A manager should be alerted. What should be configured?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Escalation rules act when cases stay open too long, for example by reassigning or notifying someone.
whyWrong: Auto-response rules reply to customers when cases are created.

sampleQuestions.question: Customers should find answers on a help site before contacting support. What is the core feature?
options: Knowledge articles published to the public or customer audience
sampleQuestions.explanation: Published knowledge articles let customers solve problems themselves, which deflects cases.
whyWrong: Case teams group people working a case.

sampleQuestions.question: Some knowledge articles are for the partner portal only. How is access controlled?
options: Article visibility settings and data categories
sampleQuestions.explanation: Article visibility and data categories decide which audiences can see each article.
whyWrong: Deleting removes them for partners too.

sampleQuestions.question: Agents repeat the same three steps when closing billing cases: send a standard email, set a status, and close. What saves time?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Macros run several steps with one click.

sampleQuestions.question: Agents want to see the full history of emails, calls and changes on a case in one place. What should they use?
sampleQuestions.explanation: The case feed shows a timeline of activity on the case.

sampleQuestions.question: A customer replies that they need a week to gather information. The resolution milestone shouldn't count that time. What should be set up?
options: Pause the milestone while the case is in a waiting-on-customer status
sampleQuestions.explanation: Entitlement processes can stop the clock for certain case statuses, so waiting time isn't counted.
whyWrong: Closing the case ends support too early.
Deleting the milestone stops tracking entirely.

sampleQuestions.question: A customer has a contract covering phone and email support for three of their products. How should this be represented?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Service contracts group the entitlements a customer has bought.

sampleQuestions.question: Agents work on several cases at once and need related records side by side. Which interface fits?
options: A standard app with one tab per page
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Service Console lets agents work in tabs and subtabs with related records alongside.
whyWrong: The Developer Console is for code.
A standard app is slower for multi-tasking.

sampleQuestions.question: When a case is created, the customer should get an email confirming receipt with a case number. What should be configured?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Auto-response rules send a reply to the customer when a case is created.
whyWrong: Milestone actions act on time limits.
Escalation rules act on overdue cases.

sampleQuestions.question: A supervisor needs to see live wait times and agent status across queues. What should they use?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Omni Supervisor shows real-time queue and agent information and lets supervisors reassign work.

sampleQuestions.question: A company wants AI to suggest the case category and the best reply to agents. What should they look at?
options: Einstein and Agentforce service AI features
sampleQuestions.explanation: Service AI features can classify cases, suggest replies and summarise conversations.
